suggestions.title: Republish your ledger — an old iPhone build is overwriting it

rationale.science: Not a physiology call, a measurement one. Adherence is the meta-lever, and adherence can only be judged from a complete log — when the record is wrong, every read downstream of it is wrong too (Alhassan 2008).
rationale.data: Your file was whole at 4:21 PM Wednesday: 47 weigh-ins, Monday's upper day and Tuesday's lower day both in, 4 approved cards. At 11:42 PM a save replaced it with a copy that stops at Monday's weigh-in and Friday's training — 2 weigh-ins, 2 sessions, 2 nights, 23 feed rows and all 4 of your approved decisions gone. The same overwrite hit twice on Wednesday afternoon and healed both times.
rationale.relationship: The culprit logs itself: an iPhone on app v4.0.11 (you're published at v4.2.9) crashed at 7:03 PM Wednesday writing sodium onto a day its stale copy doesn't contain, then saved that copy over yours 39 minutes later. Force-refresh that phone to v4.2.9 before you log anything else on it, and open the app on your current device so it republishes the whole file. Nothing is lost — every good version is still in the repo's history.

suggestions.predict: Tuesday and Wednesday's weigh-ins, both sessions, both nights and your four approved cards reappear; the trend returns to 163.9; and the lateral increment you earned Monday shows up again.

suggestions.title: Lateral machine 80 → 85 — the opener has topped its window

apply.to: Lateral machine 80 → 85 (4 sets, open at ~2 RIR)

rationale.science: Double progression: once the opener reaches the top of its rep window with reps still in reserve, load is the limiter rather than volume — and on a cut you defend and advance load instead of chasing sets (Schoenfeld 2017). ACSM's progression stand asks for 2–10% increments.
rationale.data: Your 80 lb opener has climbed three sessions running — 14,13,13 (7/20), 14,14,13,12 (7/23), 15,14,13,12 (Mon 7/27) — and 15 is the ceiling of your window, hit at 2 reps in reserve. No other lift in the programme has its opener at the ceiling.
rationale.relationship: 5 lb on 80 is 6.25%, inside ACSM's range and the smallest step your plates allow. At the 0.4-reps-per-1%-of-load slope your own app cites (Nuzzo 2024) that costs about 2.5 reps, landing the opener near 12–13 — exactly where a new load should start, so nothing has to be rebuilt.

suggestions.predict: 85 opens at 12–13 with 2 in reserve, and the four-set shape rebuilds toward 15 within two or three sessions.
